This study examines the discretization of an optimal stochastic control problem involving the parabolic differential equations, with both control variables appearing in the diffusion term and cost function terms. We propose a novel numerical scheme that ensures convergence for the associated stochastic problem. Furthermore, leveraging this approach, we develop a specific algorithm to resolve the corresponding optimal control variant.

The Telescope Array experiment has recently reported on cosmic ray data collected from 2012 to 2015, covering energies from 100 TeV up to 100 PeV. This study specifically examines the energy range above 8 EeV, where a significant modulation with a periodicity of approximately 2.5 years was detected. This observed period aligns closely with the known solar cycle. While the modulation amplitude diminishes at higher energies, the study also notes that the observed period is longer than the 1.9-year minimum found in the anisotropy signal reported by the Pierre Auger Observatory.

This study examines the charged particle spectrum in Pb-Pb collisions at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=2.76$ TeV, utilizing data collected by the ALICE experiment at CERN. The analysis focuses on events with centralities ranging from 0–10% to 90–99% and presents the nuclear modification factor ($R_{\rm AA}$) as a function of transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) for charged particles. The findings indicate that for central centralities, the $R_{\rm AA}$ drops below unity for $p_{\rm T} > 1$ GeV/$c$, while in peripheral collisions, the spectrum remains largely unaltered across the entire $p_{\rm T}$ spectrum.

We investigate the quantum mechanical system of a single particle confined to a noncommutative two-dimensional space characterized by the deformation parameter $\theta$. By applying the path integral formalism, we derive the propagator for this system and demonstrate that it adheres to the corresponding Schrödinger equation. Our derived propagator adheres to the principle of detailed balance and aligns with the results obtained via operator methods. Furthermore, we establish a direct correspondence between our findings and those of a previously published study by Datta and Roy.

The increasing availability of annotated histopathology images has enabled the creation of deep learning models capable of performing critical medical tasks, such as cancer diagnosis and prognosis. However, these models often require vast amounts of labeled data, a resource that is frequently unavailable. Federated learning (FL) offers a solution by training models across decentralized data sources without transferring the data itself, thereby preserving data privacy. This study introduces a novel FL framework designed to train deep learning models for cancer detection and grading in histopathology. Our approach addresses two key challenges: the heterogeneity in data distribution among participating institutions and the significant communication costs inherent in processing large-scale whole slide images (WSIs). To mitigate data heterogeneity, we employ a label-aware FL method that aggregates only the embeddings of soft labels rather than full image features. Furthermore, to reduce communication overhead for large WSI files, we utilize coarse-grained image patches instead of entire slides during aggregation. We evaluated our framework using five deep learning models across four institutions with real-world data, demonstrating its efficacy in delivering robust performance.

This study introduces a novel, low-complexity algorithm for synchronizing a received optical signal in submarine optical cables, which is essential for high-speed data transmission. The algorithm addresses chromatic dispersion, which degrades signal quality by distorting pulses into chirped shapes and causing inter-symbol interference. By integrating a dispersion-compensating device into the receiver, the proposed method synchronizes the signal without relying on a separate training sequence. Instead, it utilizes the inherent statistics of the transmitted data to identify the optimal synchronization point. Simulation results demonstrate that this approach outperforms existing methods in both synchronization accuracy and computational efficiency.

Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) have demonstrated exceptional performance across numerous time-series applications, such as imputation, classification, and regression. A key component of their success is the time-dilated convolution, which allows the model to capture long-term temporal dependencies. However, this mechanism can struggle with periodic signals that have very long periods. To address this, we introduce a novel architecture called Periodic Temporal Convolutional Networks (PTCNs). PTCNs utilize a novel periodic temporal convolution that effectively captures periodic patterns by dynamically adjusting dilation based on the signal's frequency. We validate the efficacy of PTCNs on multiple real-world datasets, including those for imputation, classification, and forecasting, demonstrating that they achieve state-of-the-art results.

This work presents the proof that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra defined over any field exhibits a null structure. This finding indicates that Zinbiel algebras serve as a substantial generalization of both Lie and associative algebras.

This study examines fluctuations in flow angle and magnitude within central Pb-Pb collisions at a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=2.76$ TeV, utilizing the ALICE collaboration's data from the LHC. The analysis focuses on events with $0-10\%$ centrality, specifically looking at fluctuations across event-averaged values. Results indicate that both the variance of flow angle fluctuations and the variance of flow-magnitude fluctuations are independent of transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) for $p_{\rm T} > 1$ GeV/$c$. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that event-averaged flow angle fluctuations are smaller than those predicted by hydrodynamic models, whereas fluctuations in flow magnitude align well with hydrodynamic expectations. These findings suggest that the agreement between theory and experiment for flow-magnitude fluctuations may stem from the model's accurate description of the initial spatial anisotropy in the collision.

This paper presents a new, direct proof of Sahlqvist correspondence within the framework of algebras. Sahlqvist results are pivotal in the study of modal logic, yet existing algebraic demonstrations rely heavily on complex, non-trivial tools. Our approach utilizes only fundamental concepts of universal algebra, specifically leveraging the interplay between congruences and homomorphic images. This method establishes that our findings apply to a broader class of structures than Sahlqvist formulas alone.

This study addresses the challenge of repairing table inconsistencies by defining a general framework that encompasses various table structures and logical formalisms. We introduce a suite of repair methods that balance computational efficiency with adherence to data quality metrics, which are established through the use of preference relations over possible repair outcomes. Additionally, we present efficient algorithms for computing these preferred repairs according to specific criteria.

This study introduces a time-varying extension of the Poisson INAR(1) model designed to analyze count time series exhibiting time-dependent dynamics. We establish the theoretical properties of this new specification and propose estimation methods utilizing both fixed and time-varying smoothing parameters. Furthermore, we develop a forecasting framework based on these estimators. Through a simulation study, we evaluate the proposed model's performance in terms of forecasting accuracy and its ability to detect structural breaks. Finally, we apply the time-varying Poisson INAR(1) framework to a real-world dataset representing monthly sales figures for a specific product category.

Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs) have recently enabled robotic object manipulation by predicting contact points from novel views using only RGB images. However, these models often suffer from view-dependent artifacts and limited generalization. To address these issues, we introduce NEVD, a view-conditioned equivariant neural descriptor field that integrates learned visual features with rigid pose representations. This framework ensures SE(3)-equivariance, guaranteeing consistent contact point predictions regardless of viewpoint when the input object features and pose are identical. By processing these descriptors through a lightweight decoder to generate contact points, NEVD achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard object push tasks. Furthermore, the framework's inherent equivariance allows it to generalize effectively to unseen objects and novel views without additional fine-tuning.

The SiD Detector, designed by the SIDDHEARTY collaboration, is a versatile instrument intended to investigate Standard Model physics and potential new discoveries within high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ colliders at the International Linear Collider (ILC), operating at center-of-mass energies between 200 GeV and 1.5 TeV. This design prioritizes exceptional precision in measuring Higgs boson properties, branching fractions for rare decays, and properties of light neutralinos. To achieve these scientific objectives, the SiD Detector integrates advanced technologies from both electromagnetic and hadron-catch chambers, enabling it to precisely identify electrons, photons, muons, and hadrons across a broad spectrum of momenta. This hybrid architecture delivers outstanding momentum precision of 0.05% at 50 GeV, while maintaining superior particle identification and hermetic coverage. The detector's mechanical framework is built around a lightweight, modular support system designed to accommodate the distinct requirements of its innermost layers and outer sections, ensuring optimal performance and operational flexibility.

We present new optical and near-infrared photometry for the globular cluster Tononzintla 2, revealing a population of metal-enriched stars with [Fe/H] values between +0.05 and +0.20 dex. This finding contradicts the traditional view that globular clusters are strictly single-population systems, as it demonstrates that at least some contain multiple stellar generations. The presence of these stars suggests that early supernovae enriched the cluster's interstellar medium, allowing subsequent star formation to occur with higher metallicity. Additionally, the study highlights the necessity of incorporating stellar population analysis into the characterization of candidate exoplanet host stars.

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs (AFP) has expanded significantly, yet this growth creates challenges regarding the discoverability and comprehension of its contents. To address this, we introduce a new search interface for the AFP that integrates with the existing browse system. This tool leverages the browse infrastructure to support browsing through references within proof articles. Additionally, the search functionality utilizes the semantic information encoded in the browse system's database to enhance search results. We present the design and implementation of this tool, along with an evaluation of its performance.

Using the functional renormalization group method, we examine the functional fixed point governing the universal features of phase transitions within the O(N) universality classes. We determine the location of the functional fixed point by employing the inverse flow equation with a exponential regulator. Our findings indicate that this method successfully captures the critical exponent gamma and the universal Houghton parameter across all observed universality classes. Specifically, for N=2, we find |z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma} = 1.0132 \pm 0.0002.

We introduce a new approach to analyzing the geometry of non-convex risk functions in overparameterized deep learning models. By integrating concepts from optimal transport and the Benamou-Brenier formula, we establish a connection between the optimal paths minimizing the "lossless" (risk) and the movement of probability measures. Specifically, we demonstrate that local convexity within this optimal routing minimizes the "lossless" (risk) leads to a well-conditioned Hessian for the corresponding parameter trajectory. Leveraging this geometric insight, we analyze a broad class of overparameterized neural networks and prove that the optimal trajectories minimizing the "lossless" (risk) exhibit locally convex properties around the global minimum for both classification and regression tasks. Consequently, the parameter paths associated with the "lossless" (risk) optimal solutions possess locally convex behavior in the vicinity of the global minimum for a wide range of overparameterized neural networks, encompassing both classification and regression scenarios.

Metasurfaces are now recognized as a transformative innovation in modern science and technology, defined by their ultra-thin geometry, miniaturized scale, and the ability to manipulate wavefronts through spatially varying, resonant meta-atoms. This review examines the current state of metasurface research, with a specific focus on their applications in controlling light, acoustic, and matter waves. It explores various design methodologies, including both full-wave numerical simulations and analytical approaches utilizing coupled mode theory. Furthermore, the review categorizes metasurfaces based on their underlying physical mechanisms for wave manipulation, highlighting both established and emerging technologies.

Specifically, we establish that within the space of all smooth vector fields on a compact manifold, the subset comprising those fields which linearize at a specific singular point forms a dense region. We introduce a novel Electron Correlation Potential Neural Network (eCPNN) designed to model the non-local electron correlation potential in many-electron atoms. This approach treats the potential as a function of the electron density and incorporates a unit that encodes electron angular momentum to capture the potential's angular dependence. By training on atomic data from neutral atoms and singly ionized species up to oxygen vii, the network learns to predict the correlation potential for various atomic configurations. Although developed with a limited dataset, the eCPNN demonstrates strong generalization capabilities, accurately predicting potentials for atoms and ions not included in the training set, including those with higher nuclear charges.

In this study, we utilize the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Legacy Imaging Survey to analyze the distribution of galaxies within a 1.5 Mpc radius centered on the Giant Arc, a recently identified cosmic structure. Our analysis reveals that the galaxies within the arc are spatially segregated from the surrounding field population, a finding supported by both visual inspection and quantitative metrics such as the two-point correlation function. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the arc's galaxies exhibit a significantly higher clustering amplitude than the field, a result confirmed by both visual and statistical evidence. We also present a novel method for estimating the probability of such structures arising by chance, which indicates that the likelihood of the arc forming from random fluctuations is less than 1 in 10,000. This discovery challenges the standard $\Lambda$CDM cosmological model, as the arc's size and statistical rarity appear inconsistent with current theoretical predictions.

We present a 2.5-year dataset of vertical aerosol optical depth (AOD) derived from stellar photometry, collected at the Dome C observatory in Antarctica using the AERO-CAM camera. This dataset is the longest ever obtained at Dome C and surpasses previous records by a factor of 10. Achieving this required overcoming challenges related to the site's weather patterns, the development of an automated data processing pipeline, and the refinement of analysis techniques. Our approach leverages the camera's wide field of view to aggregate numerous stars, utilizing the wide range of air masses to mitigate systematic errors, and incorporating ancillary data to enhance accuracy. These strategies yielded a high-precision AOD dataset with an annual precision of 0.002 and an inter-annual precision of 0.004. Furthermore, we analyzed the impact of volcanic aerosols on the AOD record, revealing that the 2018 eruption of the Fuego volcano in Guatemala caused an increase of approximately 0.01 in AOD that persisted for roughly 18 months.

Estimating the 6D pose of object instances within image data is typically categorized into model-based and model-agnostic methods. While current model-based approaches predominantly rely on learning-based techniques to refine pose from an initial position, model-agnostic methods have recently achieved significant success by predicting the object's implicit point cloud directly from image data. Nevertheless, existing model-agnostic frameworks often require substantial computational resources and memory, which hinders their deployment on resource-constrained devices. In this work, we propose a novel model-agnostic strategy that leverages the inherent sparsity of point clouds to deliver an efficient and accurate 6D pose solution. Specifically, we introduce a sparse point cloud generator that transforms image features into a sparse point cloud representation, which is subsequently utilized to reconstruct the object's point cloud and derive its pose. Furthermore, we present a new pose estimation network designed to accommodate the proposed sparse point cloud architecture. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on both the LPP and 6DOP benchmarks while offering significantly greater efficiency.

Peridynamics offers a robust framework for modeling discontinuities and fractures in solids, with Bond-Based Peridynamics (BBP) remaining a prominent variant due to its computational efficiency. However, the coarse grid discretization required by the fixed horizon of the nonlocal framework often introduces significant numerical dispersion and dissipation. To address these limitations, this study introduces a novel high-order numerical integration scheme for BBP that employs a refined, finer integration grid specifically for the quadrature of nodal forces, while maintaining the original coarse grid for nodal displacements. This approach yields a highly efficient algorithm that retains the inherent capability of BBP to model fractures, yet achieves enhanced accuracy through a refined force calculation process. The proposed method is validated through several benchmark problems, demonstrating its reliability and confirming that it surpasses traditional constant-coefficient BBP formulations in both accuracy and performance.

We introduce G-Lasso, a graphical modeling framework designed to estimate sparse inverse covariance matrices from multivariate Gaussian data. This approach incorporates a novel covariance-based metric for quantifying variable dependencies, offering a more meaningful alternative to traditional pairwise correlations. By leveraging this measure, we derive explicit formulas for the graph structure through graphical partial correlations and employ an adaptive method to set the regularization parameter $\lambda$. This $\lambda$ is determined by the sparsity levels of the true graph's adjacency matrix and the chosen distance metric, ensuring a robust estimation process. Furthermore, we propose a specific procedure to determine the required level of sparsity. Extensive numerical evaluations demonstrate that G-Lasso achieves superior performance in recovering the true graph topology and exhibits significant improvements in node-wise estimation accuracy compared to existing methods.

This study introduces two novel numerical approaches for simulating biomolecules: a hybrid method combining Monte Carlo and Molecular Dynamics, and a new algorithm termed "Molecular Superdynamics." Both techniques are designed to enhance the configurational sampling of molecular systems, specifically biomolecules, by significantly accelerating conformational transitions. These approaches are grounded in the principle of parallel tempering, utilizing parallel chains of simulations that share identical Hamiltonians but operate at varying temperatures. The proposed algorithms are applicable to both classical and quantum molecular models. They have been validated using two specific test cases: the rotation of a methyl group and the rotation of a phenyl ring, demonstrating their superior ability to average molecular configurations compared to traditional Molecular Dynamics and standard parallel tempering methods. The hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Superdynamics algorithms achieve this by reducing computational costs while maintaining or improving accuracy. We investigate the dynamical response of equal-mass binary black holes merging within wave dark matter environments, utilizing numerical relativity to model the interaction. Our simulations reveal that, analogous to heavier dark matter, wave dark matter generates a density wake surrounding the binary; however, the magnitude of this effect is significantly amplified for lighter dark matter waves. Furthermore, we observe that the momentum transfer from the binary to the dark matter field produces a measurable recoil velocity in the waves, a phenomenon that intensifies as the dark matter mass decreases. Additionally, our findings indicate that the energy dissipated during the merger is markedly higher when the dark matter exists in the form of waves rather than as a particle continuum.

This study examines the exponential stability of a Sturm-Liouville system featuring a coupled boundary condition within a metric graph, where one endpoint connects to a stretched Euler–Bernoulli beam. We establish the existence of suitable constants $\omega_0 > 0$ and $\delta \in (0,1]$ such that the semigroup generated by the system's associated linear operator decays exponentially for all initial data beyond a specific neighborhood of the origin defined by $\omega_0$ and $\delta$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the eigenvectors form a Riesz basis, a result which directly implies the exponential stability of the entire system.

Acoustic lenses are essential for acoustic beam steering and beamforming, with polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) being a prevalent choice. However, the high acoustic attenuation of PMMA restricts its utility in high-frequency applications. This study introduces a novel acoustic lens design utilizing Stycast 1090SI, a two-part epoxy, which exhibits significantly lower acoustic attenuation than PMMA. The design features a concave outer surface and a convex inner surface, enabling it to produce planar wavefronts when converting spherical waves from a point source into planar output. Theoretical analysis and experimental results confirm that this lens achieves a focal length of 1.5 cm and successfully generates planar wavefronts at 10 MHz. Additionally, the study demonstrates the lens's capability for beam steering, achieving a beam deflection of 30° over a 10 MHz bandwidth. Finally, the work examines the lens's bandwidth and beam-steering performance across frequencies ranging from 5 to 15 MHz.

We introduce a novel method for computing a specific type of eigenvector centrality in multilayer networks, where the significance of a node depends on both the centrality of its neighbors and the relevance of the network layers in which those connections exist. This approach is applicable to both directed and undirected networks and accommodates various scenarios regarding layer importance weights, including cases where weights are symmetric, asymmetric, or defined as functions. We provide algorithmic solutions to calculate this centrality measure and validate our methods through multiple numerical examples.

This study introduces a new approach for denoising raw images, addressing the challenge of noise removal in unprocessed sensor data. We propose a joint denoising framework that simultaneously leverages both raw and demosaiced domains. The model utilizes a shared set of weights across two interconnected networks: one operating in the raw domain and the other in the demosaiced domain. The demosaiced network is designed to demosaic raw inputs, while the corresponding reconstruction network performs the inverse operation. The training process is driven by a combined loss function consisting of individual losses for each domain and an additional cross-domain loss. Experiments conducted on both synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This work examines the R-Poincar\'{e} algebra under the condition where the central charge $Z$ is non-zero. By applying a specific coordinate transformation, we identify the resulting spacetime as de Sitter. Consequently, we derive the corresponding Newton-Wigner coordinates and the associated dispersion relation. Our findings demonstrate that this model describes a system of interacting particles moving within de Sitter spacetime.

We introduce a novel, modular framework for inferring causality from observational datasets. This system integrates various algorithms to establish both binary and multivariate causal links, while also distinguishing between causal and non-caausal relationships. Designed to support researchers in creating tailored pipelines for specific domains, our framework offers significant advantages through its extensible architecture. We demonstrate its practical application by implementing multiple state-of-the-art algorithms within this structure to analyze genomic datasets.

This study examines the dynamics of a sphere impacting a water surface, with a specific focus on the transition between the surface seal and dry spray regimes. We derive a theoretical model for the surface seal regime by analyzing the flow within the narrow gap between the sphere and the surface, incorporating the effects of surface tension. Our theoretical predictions align well with recent experimental data. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the transition from the surface seal to the dry spray regime occurs when the Bond number equals unity.

We demonstrate that generalized θ-terms, which are typically associated with anomaly cancellation, also encode information regarding global symmetries in effective field theories. This connection is substantiated by illustrating how these terms transform under the realization of global symmetries, specifically through their impact on the vacuum structure. We further examine these terms within the context of 1+1 dimensional theories featuring both continuous and discrete global symmetries, and we outline the implications of our findings for theories possessing global symmetries in higher dimensions.

This paper introduces a hardware architecture for smartphones that integrates multiple execution domains, each featuring distinct microarchitectures and security levels, to handle both security-sensitive and general tasks. By enabling secure applications to utilize dedicated, purpose-built processors, this system achieves significant performance and efficiency gains compared to relying on general-purpose cores. To manage inter-domain communication, we developed a hardware mechanism that ensures data integrity and confidentiality. Our evaluation demonstrates that this approach delivers a performance improvement of 1.5× to 2.5× and a 1.5× to 2× reduction in power consumption for security-critical workloads when utilizing domain-specific processors, while maintaining robust protection for data exchanged across domains.

This study investigates robustness in offline reinforcement learning when adversaries corrupt a subset of reward values within the training data. We introduce a new benchmark problem where corruption is bounded by an $\epsilon$-margin, defined as the maximum difference between true and observed rewards. Our analysis demonstrates that the Natural Policy Gradient (NPG) method achieves near-optimality, with sub-optimality scaling linearly to $\epsilon$. Furthermore, we examine the limits of robustness by deriving lower bounds for any algorithm facing this setting. Notably, we prove that no method can avoid a linear $\epsilon$ loss if corruption is unbounded, whereas NPG attains a superior $\sqrt{\epsilon}$ loss scaling when corruption is unbounded.

In a variation of Box Game where players cannot make choices, it is possible to predict unknown real values with high precision, even when possessing virtually no relevant data. This phenomenon occurs in the version without player selection.

Using first-principles calculations combined with dynamical mean-field theory, we investigate the electronic structure of CuFe$_2$S$_4$ (cubanite), a $d$-block transition compound known for its geological stability yet lacking comprehensive electronic characterization. Our analysis reveals an orbital-selective state where the $d_{xy}$ and $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals remain itinerant, while the $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ and $d_z$ orbitals exhibit Mott-insulating characteristics. This finding is attributed to the distinct crystal field splitting caused by the compound's specific crystallographic symmetry. Furthermore, we observe a strong coupling between the magnetic and electronic properties of CuFe$_2$S$_4$, noting that its magnetic phase transition temperature aligns closely with the onset of the Mott-insulating transition in the specified orbitals.

We propose a protocol for generating entangled photon pairs by using a single, high-quality semiconductor quantum dot as a source. This approach relies on the recombination of dark excitons, which are typically excluded from optical experiments due to their lack of direct light-matter interaction. By employing a focused, linearly polarized laser beam, we can optically access these dark states through coupling with acoustic phonons. When an initial two-level dark exciton state is prepared, the emission of one photon places the exciton into a superposition of ground and excited dark states; a subsequent recombination event then yields a second photon, resulting in an entangled photon pair. This method circumvents the primary limitations associated with utilizing bright excitons, specifically the constraints of the quantum coherence time and the breakdown of the semi-classical approximation at high excitation intensities. Our analysis indicates that entangled pairs with fidelities exceeding 99% are achievable, with a generation rate reaching approximately 1 MHz.

We have applied a tight-binding model to a two-dimensional electronic lattice with a square geometry and a square plaquette supercell, which generates four bands and two Dirac cones located at the M points of the square Brillouin zone. We have determined the precise geometric arrangement of corner and side atoms within the supercell that yields this specific configuration. Furthermore, we have derived the exact geometric parameters required to achieve perfect degeneracy at the Dirac points.

Single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) represent a novel class of nonclassical quantum states that have attracted significant interest due to their distinctive properties. This study examines the quantum characteristics of these states, including their Glauber-Sudarshan $P$-function, Mandel $Q$ parameter, quadrature fluctuations, and entanglement within a two-mode system. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of varying the initial coherent amplitude on the intrinsic features of SPCCSs. Our findings indicate that these states exhibit adjustable nonclassicality and strong entanglement, which can be regulated by the initial amplitude. Consequently, we propose that SPCCSs serve as promising candidates for applications in quantum information processing and communication.

This study introduces bivectors within the General Relativity framework, utilizing the Newman-Penrose formalism to establish a comprehensive set of identities for them. We demonstrate that these objects provide a potent computational tool for addressing problems in General Relativity, with specific applications to the Kerr spacetime and its perturbations. Additionally, we explore the geometric significance of the new bivector formalism, particularly regarding the Kerr solution.

Recent advances in artificial neural networks (ANNs) have significantly accelerated the discovery of new chemically stable compounds with desired properties, particularly within materials science. This study introduces a novel, straightforward, and highly efficient ANNs architecture designed to predict the formation energy of intermetallic compounds. By utilizing the Crystal Orbital Hybrid (COH) method, the model achieves a mean absolute error of 0.11 eV/atom on a training set of 13,500 entries and demonstrates robust performance when tested against an independent set of 5,000 compounds.

Continuous-time dynamic optimization problems are prevalent across engineering and science disciplines. While analytical solutions are often feasible, numerical approaches like collocation methods are necessary when exact solutions are unavailable. This study introduces a new framework for generating high-quality numerical solutions by integrating machine learning techniques with collocation methods. Specifically, we employ a neural network to represent the control variable within the problem formulation. We demonstrate the approach's efficacy through several illustrative examples.

Delineating esophageal tumors in CT scans poses a significant challenge for manual segmentation due to the organ's intricate three-dimensional shape, its tendency to be obscured by bone and air, and the frequent presence of artifacts. This study introduces a novel automatic segmentation framework for esophageal cancer that integrates a deep learning-based organ initializer with a level set method. The proposed deep learning model utilizes a 3D U-Net architecture trained on a dataset of 1,000 CT images containing manually annotated esophageal regions. Subsequently, a level set approach is employed to refine these initial predictions, with an energy function specifically designed to address the difficulties associated with tumor boundaries. Evaluated against 200 images not included in the training set, the method achieved a Dice Similarity Coefficient of 0.818, a Mean Absolute Distance of 1.41 mm, and a Volume Absolute Difference of 1.41 cm³. These findings indicate that the system offers robust and accurate automatic delineation of esophageal tumors.

Offshore drilling is a capital-intensive operation where well placement is critical to maximizing oil and gas recovery. To achieve this, operators rely on real-time wellbore navigation, known as geosteering, which depends on interpreting formation evaluation data. However, the inherent uncertainty in these measurements complicates the creation of robust decision-making frameworks. This paper introduces a novel approach to geosteering decisions by formulating the problem as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP). The proposed solution employs a Monte Carlo sampling technique to address the computational challenges associated with solving the corresponding POMDP. Validated against a synthetic reservoir model, the results demonstrate that this method yields superior decisions compared to conventional heuristics.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a core task in natural language processing (NLP) that has been extensively studied. While most prior research focuses on treating nested NER as an independent problem, this study proposes a new holistic framework that models the inherent nested structure of entities. Our approach employs a novel joint system that simultaneously predicts linear token-level labels and the complete set of entity spans. By utilizing a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) network for robust feature extraction, the system generates linear label predictions through a many-to-one classification scheme. Simultaneously, it applies a newly designed span labeling algorithm to identify complete entity spans via a one-to-many decoding process. This holistic architecture explicitly captures the nested relationships inherent in data. Experimental results on three public benchmarks demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art baselines, particularly in handling complex nested cases.

This work offers a geometric explanation for the $A^1$-enumeration of bitangents, which was initially provided by Xu and Zhao in 2019. We demonstrate that the multiplicity of the tropical bitangent configuration directly accounts for Xu and Zhao's original enumeration of bitangents. Furthermore, we establish a novel correspondence linking the multiplicities of tropical bitangents to those of certain non-bitangential tropical lines, thereby revealing a new geometric framework for the study of tropical bitangents.

This study introduces a novel localization algorithm designed for wireless sensor networks, specifically targeting the reduction of computational complexity and memory usage. The proposed method operates in two distinct stages. In the first stage, a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) is established among the nodes. The second stage determines the coordinates of the remaining nodes by utilizing the MST framework. Evaluation results indicate that this approach achieves high accuracy and outperforms existing methods in terms of both computational efficiency and memory consumption.

Defined as the co-occurrence of two or more languages within a single conversation, code-switching and its related phenomenon, code-mixing, are central to multilingualism research. This study introduces a novel, linguistically grounded approach to automatically detecting code-mixing in Indonesian-English dialogues. The proposed method utilizes a Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) model trained on a newly created Indonesian-English mixed-language dataset. Evaluation results indicate that this technique achieves a F1-score of 0.83, representing a significant improvement over previous methods. Furthermore, the system demonstrates robustness across various levels of code-mixing intensity. These advancements provide a more effective tool for analyzing code-mixed conversations, with potential applications in enhancing chatbots, dialogue systems, and other natural language processing tasks.

Automatic image description (AID) systems generate natural language captions that correspond to visual content, and this paper focuses on enhancing such descriptions through cross-modal paraphrase identification. In this task, the model evaluates the paraphrase relationship between an existing caption and a corresponding description provided by another model. We specifically address paraphrase identification in AID by introducing a new dataset containing pairs of descriptive captions for the same images, which are paraphrases of one another. To evaluate these paraphrase relationships, we employ the BERTScore metric, which calculates similarity based on paraphrased textual descriptions. We propose a new dataset consisting of paraphrased image caption pairs to serve as paraphrase identification in AID. To evaluate these paraphrase relationships, we utilize the BERTScore metric, which calculates similarity based on the textual descriptions of the paraphrases. Tantalum oxides ($Ta_2O_5$) are emerging as promising candidates for cancer hadrontherapy, serving as both a robust mechanical barrier and a precise Bragg peak modulator. This study employs the full-potential linearized augmented plane wave (FP-LAPW) method within the WIEN2k framework to investigate the electronic and magnetic characteristics of three specific tantalum oxide phases: $\delta-Ta_2O_5$, $\gamma-Ta_2O_5$, and $\alpha-Ta_2O_5$. Our findings indicate that the calculated lattice constants align closely with experimental data, while total energies reveal $\alpha-Ta_2O_5$ to be the most stable phase. Furthermore, the cohesive energy of $\alpha-Ta_2O_5$ is notably higher than that of the other phases, and its equilibrium volume is the smallest among them. The electronic density of states (DOS) and projected DOS (PDOS) analyses demonstrate that hybridization between O 2p and Ta 5d orbitals is the primary driver behind the material's electronic structure. Finally, our results confirm that $\alpha-Ta_2O_5$ is the sole phase exhibiting antiferromagnetic ordering.

This study examines the circulation of news, including misinformation, by analyzing the geotagging data of 11.5 million Twitter posts containing links to 1,000 stories from the 2016 U.S. presidential election. By leveraging a novel method to track misinformation propagation, the research investigates how individual traits influence the spread of false content. Specifically, it explores whether the Big Five personality dimensions affect circulation patterns and whether these impacts vary by political affiliation or state-level characteristics. The analysis reveals that while the overall circulation of misinformation is largely driven by a few viral posts, individual influence remains significant. Notably, individuals scoring high in conscientiousness tend to share false information less frequently, whereas those with high openness share it more often. Furthermore, these effects are amplified among politically moderate users and differ across states; for instance, conscientious individuals in states with a higher concentration of Republican voters circulate misinformation at even lower rates compared to those in more Democratic-leaning states.

This paper introduces a novel semi-supervised stream anomaly detection algorithm designed for high-dimensional data. It addresses the challenge of identifying suspicious events in real-time when labeled data is scarce, utilizing the fact that most available data is benign. The proposed method employs a density-based approach to handle both normal and irregular instances. It operates by constructing a density model using only clean data and subsequently classifies new stream items as anomalies if they deviate significantly from this model. Additionally, the algorithm incorporates a mechanism to continuously update the density model by integrating recently identified non-anomalous items. Experimental results on real-world datasets demonstrate that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in both accuracy and computational efficiency.

Teaching robots new skills by audio alone is challenging because natural human speech is often too vague, necessitating the use of visual cues. This study investigates whether robots can learn from audio-only demonstrations by analyzing the characteristics of human speech. We recorded speech from multiple instructors describing simple tasks, such as opening a door, and characterized the speech using three distinct feature categories: acoustic properties, linguistic structures, and pragmatic elements. Our analysis reveals that speech from different instructors exhibits significant variability across all these dimensions. Furthermore, we identified specific speech patterns that consistently signal key actions, such as the sudden pauses that indicate when to act. Finally, we demonstrate that these findings have practical applications for designing an audio-only teaching interface for robots.

This study introduces a straightforward algorithm for the uniform random generation of ordered trees that includes specific constraints on the out-degrees of nodes. These constraints are defined by a given sequence specifying permissible degree values. We demonstrate that this algorithm runs with $O(n)$ time complexity, ensuring the random sampled tree adheres to the specified degree restrictions. Furthermore, we examine several particular cases involving restricted sequences and propose algorithimicic extensions applicable to other combinatorial structures.

Conversational agents, which utilize natural language processing and machine learning to facilitate interactions through spoken or written language, have become increasingly prevalent in our daily lives. This paper introduces a new framework designed to evaluate the quality of these systems. We specifically concentrate on tasks requiring multiple dialogue turns, such as booking services or scheduling appointments, and introduce a new metric for assessing task success. Furthermore, we present a new benchmark dataset comprising 1,000 human-recorded dialogues aimed at real-world objectives. Finally, we evaluate several leading agents against this benchmark, revealing significant room for improvement in their performance.

By analyzing the current data on planetary orbits, we predict the precision achievable in measuring a hypothetical "Planet X" located at 400 AU (heliocentric distance). At this range, the median uncertainty for such a measurement is approximately 0.035 AU. Assuming the use of the same analytical methods applied to existing planets, we further estimate that the median number of required observations is only 13, with a 90% confidence interval ranging between 4 and 40 detections.

Existing research into translation memory (TM) for neural machine translation (NMT) relies almost exclusively on multilingual datasets, yet this study investigates the use of monolingual data instead. We introduce a straightforward yet effective approach that leverages a single-language corpus to construct a TM system. Our method involves training a separate NMT model on this data to create a bidirectional, language-to-self memory mechanism. Experiments conducted on the IWSLT 2017 benchmark for German-English translation demonstrate that this simple framework yields competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art TM approaches. Furthermore, our results indicate that incorporating TM from monolingual sources can actually surpass the performance of TM derived from multilingual pairs.

We investigate the likelihood of observing Hubble-flow circles with minimal variance within a standard $\Lambda$CDM cosmological framework, employing a method that accounts for both cosmic and instrumental noise. Our findings indicate that, within a single Hubble patch, approximately $10^{10}$ such low-variance circles are expected to exist. Consequently, any potential detection of a specific Hubble-patch-violating circle would likely constitute a statistical fluke rather than evidence supporting Penrose's Conformal Cyclic Cosmology, which predicts such anomalies at the boundaries of successive aeons. We further propose a technique to determine the precise distance to the centers of these observed circles.

This study introduces the concept of fractional Yambe flow, defined by $\partial_t g_{ij}=-Q(g)-\lambda\,g_{ij}$, where $Q(g)$ is the fractional curvature of order $2s$ for $s\in(0,1)$. We establish the existence of metrics within a fixed conformal class possessing constant fractional curvature, thereby generalizing results previously achieved by Brendle and the second author regarding constant classical curvature ($s=1$). Furthermore, we demonstrate the global boundedness of this flow, extending the findings of the second author and the first author's collaborator (Brendle) from the specific case of constant curvature to the broader scenario where the constant curvature condition is met over the entire domain for $s=1$.

Few-shot learning aims to classify new categories using only a handful of examples, a capability that is crucial for advancing various real-world applications. However, existing methods often struggle with new domains, a limitation likely stemming from the scarcity of domain-specific benchmarks. To address this, we introduce a new evaluation framework that provides multiple specialized few-shot learning testbeds, each containing numerous distinct domains. We evaluate seven state-of-the-art models across this framework and find that none achieve satisfactory performance. Consequently, we propose a new model that incorporates domain prototypes and domain embeddings to better capture domain characteristics. Our approach achieves significant performance gains over current leading models, particularly in challenging domains. Additionally, our framework offers a standardized set of metrics to fairly assess future model improvements.

Cross-domain recommendation (CDR) aims to enhance user profiles by leveraging data from other domains, yet most existing approaches fail to effectively utilize information from domains outside the target domain. To address this limitation, we propose MSDCR, a novel multi-domain CDR framework designed to improve user representation through collaborative recommendation across multiple domains. Specifically, MSDCR employs a multi-domain auxiliary task that generates a set of specialized recommendation models, each trained on a single domain to capture distinct user behaviors. Furthermore, the model incorporates a progressive fusion mechanism to integrate these domain-specific representations into the final user profile. Extensive experiments on two real-world datasets demonstrate that MSDCR significantly outperforms several state-of-the-art CDR algorithms.

We introduce the notion of exotic cones, which are subsets of a finite-dimensional real vector space equipped with a specific family of self-dial convex cones. This newly defined class generalizes well-known structures such as cones of positive definite matrices and enables the formulation of a distinct category of convex optimization problems. We investigate the properties of these problems, specifically addressing their dual formulations, primal and dual optimality conditions, and solution algorithms.

Automated quality control (QC) systems are essential for maintaining high standards in MRI data, yet their performance relies heavily on well-annotated datasets. Given that MRI labeling is costly and time-intensive, this study introduces a self-supervised approach for MRI QC that requires no annotations. Our method employs a ResNet-50 image classifier trained on raw, unprocessed MRI images using a self-supervised contrastive learning strategy. By applying this self-supervised model to two distinct MRI datasets, we demonstrate that it achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art automated QC methods.

This study investigates the mutual interaction between private electric vehicles (EVs) and electrical distribution systems during disruptions. It formulates a bi-level mixed-integer linear programming model where a central authority coordinates EV drivers to support the power grid, with drivers acting strategically to minimize their own travel costs while considering grid conditions. The research evaluates various coordination mechanisms, including voluntary participation, financial incentives, and regulatory mandates, analyzing how EV fleets influence grid resilience under different participation scenarios. Findings indicate that coordinated EV actions can significantly aid the grid during disruptions, yet the extent of this benefit is highly sensitive to participation rates. Consequently, while voluntary measures may be insufficient to leverage the full potential of EV fleet coordination, regulatory approaches are likely necessary to ensure robust assistance to electrical distribution systems during crises.

Intelligent autonomous mobile agents are increasingly prevalent in real-world applications, from unmanned aerial vehicles and ground systems to robotic swarms. To achieve complex missions, these agents must navigate intricate environments while adapting to dynamic conditions. This capability relies on sophisticated internal architectures that manage multiple motivations, behaviors, and learning mechanisms. This paper introduces Motivation Dynamics (MD), a novel framework designed to unify the generation of complex behaviors in autonomous mobile agents. MD functions as a biologically inspired, bi-stable dynamical system that maps environmental stimuli to competing motivations. By adjusting the system's stable states based on these stimuli, MD enables agents to execute both simple and highly complex, temporally extended behaviors. We demonstrate MD's efficacy through simulations of a quadrotor navigating a virtual canyon landscape and a swarm of agents learning coordinated behaviors in a prey-capture task. Furthermore, MD offers a computationally efficient solution for high-dimensional continuous control problems, requiring only a single stable state to represent an entire complex behavior.

We have synthesized GdSn$_3$ and CmSn$_3$ using the elemental method and evaluated their magnetic and electronic properties through magnetization measurements and first-principles calculations. Both compounds crystallize in the A15 structure and display antiferromagnetic ordering at Néel temperatures of 66 K for GdSn$_3$ and 110 K for CmSn$_3$. Furthermore, our findings reveal that GdSn$_3$ and CmSn$_3$ are compensated half-metallic antiferromagnets, exhibiting a substantial spin polarization of 99.5% at the Fermi level.

We examine the bilepton model, which modifies the standard model's gauge group to $SU(3)_C \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)'$. This study focuses on the implications of the new bilepton gauge group for the standard model's Higgs sector, specifically regarding the structure of the Higgs potential and the resulting physical Higgs spectrum. We find that the model's viability relies on the presence of additional Higgs fields beyond those in the standard model, and we determine the necessary conditions for the potential to remain bounded from below. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of the new bilepton gauge group on the physical Higgs spectrum, revealing that the model can accommodate a light Higgs boson with a mass of approximately 125 GeV.

The Orbit Sum Generator (OGS) is defined as a specific set of generators for a finite group $G$ that allows the construction of an OSG-based Cayley graph, which serves as a cover of a Cayley graph formed by any other generator set of $G$. This study focuses on identifying and characterizing the OGS for non-abelian simple groups, revealing several distinctive properties. First, the OGS is unique for any given finite group $G$. Second, it exhibits a minimal cardinality that is strictly smaller than that of any other generator set for $G$. Third, the elements within the OGS are characterized by their maximal distances from the identity element when measured on the Cayley graph derived from arbitrary generators. These findings carry significant implications for both theoretical group research and practical computational applications.

We present a novel analysis of the impact of weak gravitational lensing by dark matter halos on the magnitude dispersion of Type Ia supernovae. By utilizing a halo profile parameterized by $c\lambda$ and $w\lambda$ to describe the inner and outer regions, we determine that the inner halo density profile significantly influences the observed magnitude scatter. Our findings indicate that incorporating weak lensing effects reduces the Type Ia supernova magnitude scatter by approximately 0.015 mag, a value that aligns well with recent observational data. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the magnitude of lensing depends on the source redshift, $z_s$, and the lens redshift, $z_l$, with the maximum lensing magnitude occurring when halos are positioned at an intermediate distance between the observer and the supernova.

This paper describes the application of a new class of fully discrete numerical schemes, known as the Modified Euler-Maruyama (MEM) method, to a broad category of coercive and monotone stochastic partial differential equations (SPDE). These equations are defined by an abstract SPDE framework where the non-linear term is replaced with one satisfying specific coercivity and monotonicity conditions. The proposed MEM method is shown to be A-stable, and convergence results are established for both the case where the nonlinear term is Lipschitz continuous and scenarios involving only coercivity and monotonicity. The results are demonstrated using the two-fluid model as a concrete application.

Silicon T radiation damage centres have emerged as a promising candidate for quantum network photon-spin interfaces, offering an exceptional optical coherence time of approximately 10 microseconds. However, their suitability has been hindered by the lack of knowledge regarding their microscopic structure and the absence of a mechanism to optically initialize their states. In this study, we utilize advanced polarization-resolved photoluminescence techniques to analyze the magnetic properties of these centres. Our findings reveal that the zero-phonon line originates from two distinct configurations, each possessing an effective spin of 1 and exhibiting different magnetic behaviors. Furthermore, we demonstrate that applying uniaxial stress can optically initialize one of these configurations. This specific variant consists of a silicon interstitial paired with a substitutional germanium atom, a structure that is highly sensitive to stress. Consequently, this T centre configuration presents a viable option for creating robust, scalable, and high-performance quantum interfaces between silicon spins and photons.

Medical Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a non-invasive technique that generates high-resolution images of internal organs and tissues, enabling the detection of abnormalities such as tumors. In this study, we address the challenge of segmenting brain tumors from MR images by formulating it as a binary classification problem. Our approach employs a ResNet-50-based deep neural network, which is first trained on a dataset of non-tumor brain images to learn features for healthy anatomy. Subsequently, the model is adapted for tumor segmentation using binary classification on MRI data containing tumors. Experimental results indicate that this method achieves a Dice Coefficient of 0.818 and an accuracy of 98.8%, outperforming several state-of-the-art segmentation methods.

Stellar activity significantly influences exoplanet detection and characterization, especially in low-mass stars such as M dwarfs, which are prime targets for finding Earth-analogs. This study utilizes the 1.5-meter telescope at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory to conduct continuous, high-resolution optical and near-infrared monitoring of the active M1.5 star AD Leo for 10 days. We present a comprehensive analysis of the resulting multi-wavelength light curves, covering timescales from minutes to days. Our findings indicate that the observed activity-induced red noise in the optical spectrum is approximately 100 times greater than in the near-infrared. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the timescales of activity-induced variability in both the optical and near-infrared domains are well-modeled by a power-law power spectral density (PSD) with a slope of $\alpha \approx 2$. We also examine the relationship between stellar activity and radial velocity (RV) noise, concluding that the observed optical Ca II H&K line-index noise is insufficient to account for the measured RV fluctuations. Consequently, we attribute the remaining RV noise to the Doppler shifts caused by activity-induced spectral line broadening and asymmetry. Finally, we discuss the implications of these results for future exoplanet research.

This study introduces a novel, bidirectional link quality estimation method designed for Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) to address the challenge of asymmetric link characteristics. By integrating a specific data aggregation algorithm, the proposed approach enhances overall network performance. Experimental results confirm that this technique effectively improves the accuracy of link quality assessments.

Object detection in images is typically classified into three groups based on contextual usage: one-to-one detectors, one-to-many detectors, and scene detectors. This study focuses specifically on one-to-one detectors, known as fine-grained detectors, which identify and classify specific object categories within an image. Although existing methods for these detectors have achieved impressive results, they often rely on extensive manual annotations and are prone to overfitting. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel framework called Contextualized Self-Supervised Learning (CSL) designed for one-to-one detectors. The proposed method leverages self-supervised training to enhance feature extraction and incorporates a contextualized mechanism to mitigate the effects of overfitting. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques on the CUB-200-2011 dataset.

This paper presents a new approach to establishing the existence of multiple solutions for a Kirchhoff type elliptic system characterized by multiplicity. The proposed method diverges from traditional frameworks by employing a specific construction of the linking geometry, thereby circumventing the requirement for the Cerami condition to satisfy the Palais-Smale compactness constraint. Instead, the authors utilize an alternative compactness assumption alongside variational techniques grounded in Fountain theorem and its variants.

This study examines concentration of measure for functions of independent random variables within the context of matrix-val functions. We derive new inequalities extending the product form of Brascamp-Lippschmid (BL) to scenarios where some functions are strongly Rayleigh. Specifically, we establish that the strong Rayleigh property is sufficient to obtain BL-type results even when certain functions depend on multiple arguments. As a primary application, we derive explicit bounds for the joint tail probabilities of independent Gaussian variables, addressing a problem posed by Dembo, Shalev, and Zeitouni. Additionally, we address the query raised by Dembo, Shalev, and Zeitouni regarding the existence of a uniform constant $C$ such that for any $n \times n$ orthogonal matrix $U$ and any Gaussian vector $g \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the probability $P(\max_{i,j} U_{ij} g_i g_j \ge t) \le C e^{-t^2/2}$ holds for all $t > 0$.

This study examines dihadron production within deep inelastic scattering at leading twist order, specifically within the TMD factorization framework. We derive the dihadron fragmentation function (TDDFF) by applying a Fourier transform to the TMDFF, and subsequently calculate the unpolarized semi-inclusive hadron production cross section at leading order. Our analysis demonstrates that the azimuthal asymmetry, quantified by $\theta_R$, offers a means to access TDDFFs at substantial transverse momentum. Furthermore, we establish a direct relationship between this azimuthal angle and the transverse momentum of partons in the initial hadron, indicating that measuring $\theta_R$ allows for the determination of parton transverse momentum at higher precision.

This work examines the Fock transformation, a deformation of Special Relativity that preserves the Poincaré algebra's semi-direct product structure. We demonstrate that this transformation can be decomposed into a sequence of simpler transformations, each corresponding to a specific deformation of the Lorentz group. We also derive the inverse transformation and establish its connection to the Bimodal Lorentz transformation. Furthermore, we show that the Fock transformation is a linear mapping, whereas the associated Bimodal Bimodal transformation is nonlinear. Finally, we confirm that the Fock transformation is a valid representation of the Deformed Lorentz Boost.

This expository article outlines the parametrization of conjugacy classes within the symplectic group $Sp(2n, \mathbb{C})$ utilizing specific pairs of symplectic modules. It further details the computation of characteristic polynomials and provides formulas for integrating metaplectic representations over conjugacy classes.

We introduce a new recommendation task focused on completing entities within the Wikipedia knowledge graph. Current approaches to this problem typically rely on converting knowledge graph structures into natural language sentences and applying pre-trained language models to predict missing components. In contrast, our method utilizes a graph neural network (GNN) to generate embeddings for each entity. We evaluate our approach against existing methods using the WikiRC dataset, demonstrating that our model achieves superior performance. Additionally, we provide an analysis of the learned embeddings and a practical application showing how these recommendations can enhance the functionality of entity recommendation systems in Wikipedia.

Patients awaiting kidney transplantation often face complications due to immunologically incompatible donors. While current methods for generating compatible pairs rely on crossmatching donor lymphocytes against recipient serum, this approach is hindered by the presence of preformed antibodies that are not detected by serology. To address this, we developed a novel microarray-based technology capable of simultaneously profiling thousands of HLA antigens. By utilizing this array to characterize both donor and recipient HLA types, we can accurately predict the specific antigens responsible for any incompatibility. Furthermore, this method enables the identification of the corresponding anti-HLA antibodies in the patient's serum. Consequently, this approach offers a robust means of predicting the antigens involved in transplant rejection.

Implicit copulas are increasingly preferred for modeling dependence structures in high-dimensional settings due to their ability to circumvent the challenges associated with copula parameter dimensionality. Nevertheless, the theoretical foundations regarding the convergence of dependence structures based on implicit copulas remain largely unexplored. This study introduces a novel estimator for the dependence structure derived from implicit copulas by employing a kernel-based approach. We establish the consistency of this proposed estimator, and furthermore, extend our findings to provide a broadened framework applicable to a broader class of implicit copulas.

In Natural Language Processing, word representations are typically learned from the distributional patterns of terms across a corpus. This study introduces a novel approach to understanding the relationship between these term frequencies and their corresponding embeddings. We demonstrate that certain pre-trained embeddings can be approximated by a function derived solely from the input text's term frequency distribution, utilizing only a few hyperparameters. Furthermore, we show that these embeddings effectively cluster documents sharing similar high-frequency vocabulary. Finally, we utilize this insight to develop a new document representation method that learns directly from term counts, eliminating the need for an initial corpus of pre-trained embeddings.

This study introduces SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM, which serve as SISO-FM and MISO-FM counterparts, respectively. These schemes offer advantages such as reduced hardware complexity, lower costs, and simpler designs. Furthermore, this paper derives the optimal bit allocation and power distribution strategies for both SISO-OFDM and MISO-FM systems operating under average power constraints.

This study presents a new numerical approach for simulating two-phase flows involving phase change within complex geometries. The methodology combines a front-tracking technique for phase boundaries with a finite volume scheme for the bulk domain. Bulk governing equations are discretized using a coupled formulation of the momentum and energy equations, while interface dynamics are governed by the level-set equation, with curvature derived from the coupled momentum formulation. To accommodate moving boundaries, the framework employs a hybrid grid system that integrates Cartesian background structures with body-fitted meshes. This integration is managed through a coupling strategy that ensures consistency in both temperature and energy across the interface. The proposed model is validated against three benchmark cases: a flat interface undergoing phase change, a two-phase Rayleigh-Taylor instability, and phase change occurring within a complex boundary configuration.
